claims.claim: For fixed quiescent history and width-four iid root law, the sector probability vector is sufficient and identifiable for the one-wave sector count law (multinomial). Equal coarse count/mark states need not give equal sector probability, with exact actual native witnesses. Full root N,W,prior and clock determine current PUCT root scores, not deeper mark dynamics.
claims.limit: Fixed clean registered selectors and chosen sectors. Coarse pairs share same root/evaluator/time; no full root-count/NW collision in samples, so full-tree/mark sufficiency not established. Repeated pair counts not independent samples.

claims.claim: For any fixed finite trajectory ensemble with clock-dependent coarse conditional projections, the exact two-time conditional propagator has a discrete nonstationary signed memory expansion; recursive kernels equal the orthogonal-residual projection products. Full recurrence exactly reconstructs the direct law.
claims.limit: Finite empirical projection, not autonomous Markov closure or a native microscopic memory force; no arbitrary population transfer. Truncated signed kernels may require simplex projection.

claims.claim: Adaptive multinomial sector counts admit predictable compensation, exact quadratic variation and exponential martingale. Dyadic normalized compensated covariance equals expected averaged predictable covariance; no independent-wave assumption. Actual R76/R77 sector laws and frozen beta-zero reference verify the finite conditional identities.
claims.limit: Five finite sizes, two densities, three beta, separate cohorts. Empirical variance and exponential estimates not all calibrated; no native CLT, physical universality, stationary correlation time or spatial RG fixed point.
